title: Colomba di Pasqua
subtitle: Italian Easter dove bread: a rich, risen loaf shaped like a dove, glazed with almonds and sugar
excerpt: Colomba di Pasqua is the Italian Easter equivalent of panettone: a very enriched, lightly flavoured bread risen to an airy softness, glazed before baking with a rough almond and egg-white paste that sets to a crisp, slightly bitter crust. It is shaped into a dove, though it softens into an irregular oval as it proofs.
sourceNotes: Colomba di Pasqua (Easter dove) became a mass-market product in Italy from the 1930s when Dino Villani, advertising director of Motta, adapted the panettone mould and recipe for Easter. The home version follows the structure of panettone dough but with orange blossom water, candied peel, and the characteristic almond glaze. Standard Italian pasticceria literature documents the method.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze completely cooled, wrapped in baking paper then cling film. Thaw at room temperature for 3 to 4 hours.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Colomba keeps for 5 to 6 days wrapped at room temperature. The texture is best on days 2 and 3 as the enriched crumb relaxes.

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: Conventional oven, 170 degrees Celsius. Fan oven: 155 degrees Celsius. Lower shelf. Cover with foil after 20 minutes to prevent the almond glaze over-browning.

glossaryTerms.definition: The traditional form for colomba di Pasqua: two logs of dough arranged in a cross, the longer piece for the body (head to tail) and the shorter, wider piece for the wings. The shape puffs and rounds during proofing and baking; the finished loaf reads as a dove when seen from above.

content.text: Colomba uses the same sponge method as kulich: a portion of the flour, all the yeast, and some milk ferment together for an hour before the remaining ingredients are added. This gives the yeast a head start before the butter and eggs slow it down. The
is formed from two pieces of dough arranged in a cross on the tray; the almond glaze and pearl sugar are added just before baking.
Combine the sponge ingredients into a batter. Cover and leave for 45 to 60 minutes until very bubbly and doubled.

Add the flour, sugar, salt, eggs, egg yolks, vanilla, and orange blossom water to the risen sponge. Mix until a rough dough forms, then knead for 8 to 10 minutes until smooth. Add the softened butter in three additions, kneading each addition in fully. Knead for a further 8 minutes until the dough is smooth, glossy, and elastic.
Flatten the dough, scatter the mixed peel over it, fold and press to incorporate. Cover and leave at room temperature for 1 to 1.5 hours until doubled.

Divide the dough: two-thirds for the body, one-third for the wings. Shape the larger piece into a fat sausage and the smaller into a shorter, wider sausage. Arrange them in a cross on a lined baking tray. Proof for 1.5 hours until noticeably puffed.
Mix the ground almonds, icing sugar, and egg white into a thick paste. Spread it over the entire surface of the proofed colomba. Scatter pearl sugar and flaked almonds over the glaze.

Bake at 170 degrees Celsius for 40 to 45 minutes. Cover loosely with foil after 20 minutes. The colomba is done when an instant-read thermometer reads 90 to 92 degrees Celsius at the centre. Cool on a wire rack for at least 1 hour before slicing.
